summary: quote returns SQL literal text representing a value.
documentation: quote returns SQL literal text representing a value. Text is single-quoted with internal apostrophes doubled; NULL becomes the text NULL. A blob becomes a hexadecimal literal. It is useful for inspecting values rather than constructing executable application queries.
inputs: samples(id INTEGER, value), with no declared affinity for value.
returns: id and literal text, ordered by id.
caution: Use bound parameters for real database input. quote is not a replacement for parameter binding, and embedded NUL characters in text have special truncation behavior excluded here.
scenarios: Inspect literal representations in a database debugging report.
Explain how text and NULL differ in a SQL teaching example.
Preview blob and number values in a local export audit.
title: Inspect SQL literal representations
problem: Return id and quote(value) AS literal from samples, ordered by id. Text contains no NUL characters. Preserve the distinction between text NULL and SQL NULL.
hint: quote returns text even for a SQL NULL value.
goal: Use quote() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
starter:
-- Write one SELECT or WITH query against the supplied tables.
SELECT 1;
